policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word order only: 'went out from the temple, and was going on his way' renders the same words in either order; English word order follows the translator, not the Greek.
ASV 'But he answered and said unto them' renders the participle (ho de apokritheis eipen) and names no subject; the alternative supplies 'Jesus', which the ASV does not have.
Word order only: both readings give 'all these things'.

Presence or absence of the article is not renderable in English; 'the end of the world' is unchanged either way. The alternative_rendering note concerns English wording ('consummation of the age') and the greek_gloss note concerns parousia, so neither maps to this unit.
ASV 'for these things must needs come to pass' has no 'all'; the alternative adds panta, which the ASV would render.
ASV lists only 'famines and earthquakes'; the alternative adds kai loimoi ('and pestilences'), a lexical item absent from the ASV text.
Orthographic variation of the same perfect participle; 'standing' renders either spelling.
Both prepositions with the accusative yield 'unto the mountains'; the English does not distinguish epi from eis here.
Aorist and present imperative of the same verb; both render 'not go down'.
ASV 'his cloak' is singular, matching to himation; the alternative is the plural ta himatia, which the ASV renders elsewhere as 'garments'.
ASV 'so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect' is active with 'the elect' as object; the alternative planasthai is passive/middle ('so that even the elect should be led astray').
The added kai is adverbial ('so shall also be'); the ASV's 'so shall be the coming' neither requires nor excludes it, since an adverbial kai is routinely left unrendered.
ASV opens the sentence 'Wheresoever the carcase is' with no connective; the alternative adds gar, which the ASV renders as 'for' when present.
Presence of the article before ouranoi is not renderable; 'in heaven' is unchanged.

ASV text reads 'with a great sound of a trumpet', which requires phones (salpingos phones megales); the mapped textual_variant note assigns the reading without phones ('with a great trumpet') to the margin as what many ancient authorities read.
Article only; 'from one end of heaven to the other' is unchanged. The verse's textual_variant note is mapped to the salpingos unit, not to this article.
Word order only: both give 'all these things'.
Recitative hoti after 'I say unto you' is not rendered in the ASV either way.
Singular and plural of the same future verb; English 'shall pass away' is invariant for a compound subject.
ASV text has 'neither the Son'; the mapped textual_variant note ('Many authorities, some ancient, omit neither the Son') places the omission in the margin, so the text follows the longer reading.
ASV 'but the Father only' has no possessive; the alternative adds mou, which the ASV renders as 'my' when present.
ASV opens 'And as were the days of Noah'; 'And' renders de, whereas gar is rendered 'for' in the ASV (cf. its 'For as in those days' in the next verse).
The added kai is adverbial ('so shall also be'); the ASV's 'so shall be the coming' does not settle it, since an adverbial kai is routinely left unrendered.
hos and hosper are rendered alike by 'as'; the ASV's 'For as in those days' does not distinguish them.
ASV 'in those days which were before the flood' has the demonstrative 'those', which renders ekeinais; the base reading has only 'in the days'.
Simplex and compound form of the same verb; both render 'giving in marriage'.

The English renders 'and' at both clause joints ('and they knew not', 'and took them all away') and no adverbial 'also' before 'the coming', so the ASV does not show which kai this unit covers or whether it stood.
Word order only: 'Then shall two men be in the field' renders either arrangement.
Article before heis is not renderable; ASV has bare 'one' either way.
Article before heis is not renderable; ASV has bare 'one' either way.
ASV 'grinding at the mill' renders mylo (the mill itself); mylon means the mill-house, which the ASV does not have.
ASV 'ye know not on what day your Lord cometh' renders hemera; the alternative reads hora, which the ASV renders 'hour' (as at v. 44).
Word order only: 'in an hour that ye think not' renders either arrangement.
ASV 'his lord' is an ordinary rendering of the articular ho kyrios for a relational noun in this context, so the possessive does not require the added autou.
oiketeia and therapeia are both the body of household servants; ASV 'his household' renders either.
Aorist and present infinitive of the same verb; both render 'to give'.
Word order only: both give 'so doing'.
ASV 'My lord tarrieth' has no complementary infinitive; the alternative adds elthein ('delayeth to come'), which the ASV would render.

ASV 'and shall begin to beat his fellow-servants, and shall eat and drink' makes the eating and drinking a second finite clause, not a further complement of 'begin', which excludes the infinitives of r02; the remaining two readings differ only in punctuation, which the English cannot settle.
